## Jacobian and Keller maps

Polynomial Keller maps, their fibres, monodromy and boundary geometry.

**Authored assessment:** Explicit ordinary characteristic-zero Keller collisions give an internal failure of the unrestricted Jacobian conjecture under the retained proofs. JC2, universal classifications and minimum bounds remain open; external review remains separate. Cubic homogeneous cube-zero Jacobians now have sharp dimension-independent inverse degree29; the cubic length-three shuffle threshold is exactly15. Higher nilpotency-index cases remain open. A standalone48-variable rational cubic now attains inverse degree29 with exact Jacobian nilpotency index3; its complete direct symbolic check takes under one second. At cubic Jacobian nilpotency index4 an explicit58-variable map has inverse degree207, so every dimension-uniform bound is>=207; a uniform bound or an unbounded family remains open. Small7/9 maps obstruct affine/quadratic fibre reduction over cube-zero bases in every linear frame. The explicit index-four block now has exact localized scalar-extension criteria: after its degree207 coordinate, independence ofS plus the pre-S joint-kernel condition is necessary and sufficient; independence alone fails. Infinite parallel repeatability remains open. The homogeneous exact-index17 collision now yields explicit triangular jet families of unbounded inverse degree, so all-path cubic uniformity is false; fixed4 remains open. A separate repeatable index4 block has exact inverse reset and bounded degree207, and two full cubic-helper restart fibres admit no old polynomial correction.

## Factorial moments and rigidity

Factorial moment functionals, composition rigidity and Strong Factorial families. Coefficient-uniform windows are proved for all quadratic phases in every dimension. Ordinary two-monomial coprimality in arbitrary dimension first remains at terminal fifteen. The initial homogeneous bivariate trinomial window has a finite global degree reduction and is the immediate completion priority. The arbitrary-dimensional two-monomial residual still contains infinitely many exponent profiles.

**Authored assessment:** Priority: finish the initial homogeneous bivariate trinomial window at orders 1, 2, 3. A computable absolute degree bound reduces every possible failure to a finite exact residual; the bound and full residual are unevaluated, so practical feasibility is unknown. A uniform resultant/remainder sign proof is an alternative finish. Treat the arbitrary-dimensional two-monomial obstruction at exceptional Gaussian limits as a separate research project. Ordinary univariate binomial Strong Factorial is proved at every terminal over every characteristic-zero field. The proof combines the terminal-through-24 theorem, the exact prime, Newton and modular certificate through terminal 3149, and the uniform Padé cutoff at terminal 3150. For arbitrary ordinary multivariate binomials, terminals 2 through 14 and every terminal at or above a computable absolute cutoff are proved. Both-private supports are covered in every degree, and one-private supports are covered when the private total exponent is at least five. For 2<=P<=4 the registered sufficient lower bounds on shared curvature are 73/9, 37/6, 38/9 respectively. Unrestricted coprimality for the remaining multivariate supports and the larger-support conjecture remain open.

## Dixmier and Weyl algebras

Formal Weyl lifts, scalar mate obstructions, finite centralizers and exact quantum division spectra.

**Authored assessment:** All-order formal lifting, low-order DC1 automorphisms and scoped obstructions remain internally established. Canonical graded scalar Long lifts require spatial degree at least 28 with arbitrary parity; degree 27 is the sharp minimum through h5. The admitted XQ Airy source datum gives a matrix jet through h4 at degree 25, but its entire prescribed-first-coefficient family fails at h5 through degree 26. Three crossing coordinates give a one-order covariant correction test without a uniform bound. Actual centered polynomial Weyl pairs have zero mixed symmetric Weyl coefficient, and their ordinary rational differential intertwiners are scalar. Differential orders ten and eleven force generation; proper pairs have composite orders at least twelve. Global polynomial admission, higher critical faces and arbitrary Weyl-division transport remain open. No bounded full Long lift or DC1/DC2 resolution is obtained.

## Meridional rank

Knot-group representations, branched-cover bounds and explicit sharp families.

**Authored assessment:** The prime four-bridge family has ar_C3<mr=bridge4, hyperbolic covers/exteriors, cycliccoverH1 and sharporbifoldtorsionrank4. Exact Fox identities exclude all scalar models and all models through the fixed A8 and A8 x C2 quotients, in every characteristic. Ordinary knot-group rank, other coefficientmodels, remaining known-family/priority boundaries and fullMRC stayopen. Every finite metabelian quotient of each Kn is generated by at most two elements. Verified symmetry proves exact ordinary rank3 for the32 named knot groups and for all closed double-cover groups of Kn, and bounds ordinary ranks of Gamma_n and G_n between3 and4. For the explicit protected-U knots on b strands with k disjoint blocks, ar_C<=b−k without any preserved form. Every such returning-tail double-transposition coloring has support v<=2b−2k+2, so the standard support bound can certify at most gap one. A hyperbolic prime gap-two realization remains open.

## Arithmetic fibres, discriminants and restricted-prime sums

Constructive finite etale fibres, arithmetic failures and discriminant geometry. Two companion preprints are published on Hexagon: general pointwise quadratic-value and splitting-semigroup correlations, and independent exact primitive-norm sumset classifications at discriminants -3,-7,-8,-11. The specified diagonal Pade three-halves witness sequence, over all degrees selected per pair, has only O(T^(1+epsilon)) compatible unit kernel pairs at N comparable to T^5 and height<=4T^2. Actual bounded-degree rational witness families admit coefficient-uniform and fixed-family kernel counts, including prime and separated-coarse-modulus/cube-free refinements. Actual auxiliary Q-curves have an exact remainder-content/effective-modulus bridge; an economical full long-complement cover is still open. Every seventh-power prescribed targetN=M^7 has r(N)<<N^(2/7+epsilon), including noncoprime positive squarefull summands, via a coefficient-uniform cube-divisor estimate. Every actual cube divisor q^3|N controls all original square-full pairs by N^epsilon*(q+sqrt(N)/q^(3/4)). A common-kernel-gcd refined square-quotient weight gives another coefficient-uniform actual C6 tail, with an explicit reverse route to the previous quotient tail. Elementary real-quadratic norm recovery removes the kernel-gcd coefficient loop and yields stronger selected-cycle weighted tails, with an explicit chi coefficient gain. Fixed mixed powers2<=k<j,3|j,k∤j admit kernel-gcd recovery and chi-sensitive actual path/cycle weights, using casewise norm/Thue lifting; the square-cube case has a separate direct route. A conditional coarse-global-triple to actual-path transfer and exact majorant comparison identify a limited exponent-only barrier; they supply no prescribed-sum improvement. Dual graphs give uniform positive-coefficient counts for unrestricted products of two fixed powers; the squarefull3/10result has a separatefullscope alternate proof. Exact-five carriers give stronger restricted sectors for3-full sums. Coherent six-cycles give the unconditional all-target bound r3(N)<<N^(33/134+epsilon), resolving the positive-saving target; the stronger carrier support-capacity estimate remains open. On the original marked-octic parameter line, MO2a gives ≫ X^(1/4)/(log X)^2 imaginary quadratic fields of class 3-rank at least three, improving the explicit Kulkarni–Levin Theorem 1.5 bound; proof review and current-record comparison remain open. The marked octic also gives simultaneous real and imaginary-mirror class 3-rank bounds three and four, at least forty complex cubic fields of a common fundamental discriminant, three positive-rank elliptic twists and ≫ X^(1/12)/(log X)^2 distinct fields. Every nonzero rational scaling of its genus-eleven cubic cover has exactly four rational three-torsion directions; real class rank four remains open.

| [Macroscopic valuation grids leave at least the summed nonatomic radical mass](arithmetic/ABC_SECANT_ENDPOINT_TRANSFER.md) | proved | proved | For each fixed b>0, along a near-full product relation and any adaptive q>=b/L the sum of the pure radical exponents on valuations not divisible by q has liminf at least the sum of the selected input nonatomic masses, which is at least m/3. | [One compressed valuation core suffices for the weighted two-column codegree](arithmetic/ABC_COMPRESSED_CORE_WEIGHTED_CODEGREES.md) | proved | proved | Two primitive columns with nonzero determinant and one eligible compressed original target core per row have O(X^(B+eta lambda+epsilon)) rows per fixed cofactor on that edge or per fixed reduced cofactor ratio. | [A Latin prime dictionary prevents a ratio deficit from marginal capacities alone](arithmetic/ABC_COMPRESSED_CORE_WEIGHTED_CODEGREES.md) | proved | proved | In an abstract complete balanced bipartite graph assign a distinct prime to each modular row-plus-column label. | [Counting exponent is strictly below the positive-scale mass on two letters](arithmetic/ABC_IMBALANCED_PRODUCT_RADICAL_GROWTH.md) | proved | proved | In a height-first primitive family of positive normalized exponent d, track the full exact degree measures on two letters and a full divisor of the third with bounded normalized radicals. | [Imbalanced products have arbitrarily large fresh-radical floors and low-order weight](arithmetic/ABC_IMBALANCED_PRODUCT_RADICAL_GROWTH.md) | proved | proved | Under the imbalanced product hypothesis, for each fixed B>0 the fresh radical cap X^(BL) is power-small with the corresponding fixed weight ratio. | [Exclusion of a pair with excessive low-order radical mass](arithmetic/ABC_IMBALANCED_PRODUCT_RADICAL_GROWTH.md) | proved | proved | There are absolute positive sigma, theta, delta,L0 so that in the primitive height shell each letter radical <=X^((1/3+delta)L) and a pair radical mass at orders vL<=sigma at least 1/3-theta imply a count O(X^((1/3-delta)L+epsilon)) for fixed 0<L<=L0. The conclusion applies at arbitrary total nonatomic mass. |
| [A deficit in the live nonatomic sum excludes bounded radical records](arithmetic/ABC_IMBALANCED_PRODUCT_RADICAL_GROWTH.md) | proved | proved | For synchronized product weights along a near-full output sequence, when the live input pairs (positive limiting weight on output scale) have combined nonatomic radical strictly below m/3, no bounded-radical full divisor of the target can leave a cofactor of vanishing numerical height. | [Hensel packing bounds high orders on small primes of a powered binary form](arithmetic/ABC_IMBALANCED_PRODUCT_RADICAL_GROWTH.md) | proved | proved | For fixed K,L and prescribed polynomial-height alpha,beta, primitive pairs of height at most X with the full part of alpha*u^K+beta*v^K on primes p<=X^(tau L), p not dividing K alpha beta, v_p>=kappa K/L larger than 2X^2 have count O(X^((tau+2/(kappa K))L+epsilon)). Each selected modulus branch packs the original primitive ratio. |
| [A fixed affine target ratio power class has subpower multiplicity](arithmetic/ABC_RECTANGLE_POWER_CLASS_DEFECT.md) | proved | proved | For independent polynomial-height integer affine forms with positive values at most X^K, the multiplicity of any fixed q-power class of their ratio is O_K,epsilon(X^epsilon) uniformly over q>=2. Includes both orientations of each nonzero residue valuation, fixed by support assignments. A prescribed excluded prime pool and outside q-defect bound Z give O(Z X^epsilon) rows over all adaptive orders. |
| [Two active independent affine coefficients suffice in a product power class](arithmetic/ABC_RECTANGLE_POWER_CLASS_DEFECT.md) | proved | proved | For finitely many independent affine targets with prescribed exponents, a fixed product q-power class has subpower occurrences when two active target exponents survive modulo a common prime divisor of the effective orders. Freeze the bad determinant supported parts before applying the two-column norm count. |
| [Affine target rectangles with low adaptive power defect have a star bound](arithmetic/ABC_RECTANGLE_POWER_CLASS_DEFECT.md) | proved | proved | Given a polynomial-height excluded prime pool per reference star, the ordered rectangles having full target cross-ratio defect <=Z at any order q>=2 are at most O(Z X^epsilon) times the number of ordered two-edge stars. | [Edgewise adaptive power defects give a strict affine graph bound](arithmetic/ABC_RECTANGLE_POWER_CLASS_DEFECT.md) | proved | proved | For independent affine target columns, prescribed fixed coefficients and prime pools, and off-grid radical <=Z on each edge, M=O(X^epsilon(A+B sqrt(A) Z)) for A rows and B columns. Covers edge-dependent orders, column coefficients and common row factors under the stated height or order hypotheses. For equal balanced part exponent c, exact powers give exponent 3c/2. |
| [Minimal target repairs cannot be multiplicatively separable on a dense affine graph](arithmetic/ABC_RECTANGLE_POWER_CLASS_DEFECT.md) | proved | proved | At target height <=X^K, r-full least target repairs with rectangle r-defect <=Z outside reference pools give O(Z X^(2K/r+epsilon)) times the number of stars. | [A fixed multilinear norm value recovers all primitive input directions](arithmetic/ABC_TENSOR_NORM_FRESH_RADICALS.md) | proved | proved | The norm of a basis-linear function of m independent ratios in an integral degree-(m+1) basis recovers O(X^epsilon) possible tuples per nonzero value, uniformly in moving fields and bases of fixed polynomial conjugate height. | [Independent multivariable norms each pay the full tuple exponent in joint fresh radical](arithmetic/ABC_TENSOR_NORM_FRESH_RADICALS.md) | proved | proved | For fixed m balanced slots and s degree-(m+1) norm forms from integral bases of polynomial conjugate height, assume all pairwise homogeneous resultants in every slot are nonzero. Outside all original prime supports and any fixed polynomial-height pool, a joint radical cap n^(sm/3-eta) gives a power-smaller tuple count. Resultants and Loomis-Whitney first fix the joint shared radical; the norms then count separately. Explicit shifted bases fulfill every resultant hypothesis. |
| [The third radical cap gives a two-ninths count on a moving affine line](arithmetic/ABC_AFFINE_SLICE_RADICAL_COUNTS.md) | proved | proved | For primitive triples in a height shell with each letter radical cap X^(l_T L), a prescribed weighted relation pU+qV=t with all coefficients nonzero and polynomial height gives a count with coefficient (l_U+l_V)/3 in base X^L, plus arbitrarily small allowances. If the weighted shift is shorter by X^tau the coefficient is min(l_U,l_V)/2. A moving noncoordinate affine line at total cap X^L therefore gives coefficient 2/9. |
| [An affine slice at coefficient two ninths forces one macroscopic prime per letter](arithmetic/ABC_AFFINE_SLICE_RADICAL_COUNTS.md) | proved | proved | In balanced caps 1/3 on each letter, on a noncoordinate affine line with limiting coefficient 2/9, all three exact scaled degree laws equal (1/9) delta_0+(2/9) delta_(9/2). Each positive-scale portion is carried, up to vanishing normalized radical, by one prime after discarding power-smaller exceptional sets. Excludes stripped height collapse and escaped moments. |
| [The balanced Pell slice has small-budget coefficient one sixth at fixed offsets](arithmetic/ABC_AFFINE_SLICE_RADICAL_COUNTS.md) | proved | proved | For the positive family m,m+kappa,2m+kappa, any fixed nonzero integer kappa gives exponent (1/6+zeta)lambda+epsilon at all sufficiently small fixed budgets, including nonprimitive triples by fixed divisor splitting. For a polynomial-height moving kappa and primitive rows the uniform coefficient is 2/9 and is 1/6 under a fixed relative height gap. Summing over offsets \|kappa\|<=X^(theta L) gives coefficient 1/6+theta+zeta. |
| [Balanced endpoints require large nonconstant weighted-shift dictionaries](arithmetic/ABC_AFFINE_SLICE_RADICAL_COUNTS.md) | proved | proved | A near-full balanced family in base n=X^L requires projection exponent at least 1/9 in any fixed weighted form pU+qV with nonzero coefficients on different letters, uniformly at polynomial height. The floor rises to 1/6 for uniform relatively short weighted shifts. A union of noncoordinate affine lines below the corresponding capacity receives a strict count saving. |
| [Near-quadratic linear tripartite graphs can exclude balanced six-cycles](arithmetic/ABC_BALANCED_LATIN_TRADE_OBSTRUCTION.md) | proved | proved | A balanced 4-cycle is impossible in a proper complete-label projection, and balanced six-cycles lift exactly to 3x3 grids. KSW v2 therefore gives abstract near-endpoint graphs avoiding these cycles and any nonzero signed incidence cancellation supported on at most seven edges. Eight-edge support must be induced on twelve vertices in this construction. |
| [A dense linear tripartite graph forces a bounded signed incidence relation](arithmetic/ABC_BALANCED_LATIN_TRADE_OBSTRUCTION.md) | proved | proved | At E=N^(2-o(1)) and three part caps N there is an integer incidence relation on at most twelve edges with coefficients of absolute value at most two. Two faithful three-step paths in the ordered common-center pair graph telescope to the same endpoint vectors. |
| [Exact addition forces a simultaneous arithmetic parallelogram on the three letters](arithmetic/ABC_BALANCED_LATIN_TRADE_OBSTRUCTION.md) | proved | proved | With actual distinct integer labels and a+b=c on each edge, if E>=K N^(7/4) then there are at least a constant times E^10/N^15 faithful matching pairs as in BT2. For a near-full complete-label family this gives N^(5-o(1)) configurations, at a sharp combinatorial exponent. |
| [The dual Fermat cone has square-root cancellation at disjoint shifted branches](arithmetic/ABC_THREE_PRIME_FERMAT_NOISE.md) | proved | proved | In a generic direction on the degree-d Fermat cone, the normalized additive Fourier coefficient along a line is the centered fibre count of a tame degree-d Fermat projection. Up to four shifts with disjoint finite branch sets have complete additive correlation O_d(sqrt p), including a linear additive twist. |
| [Twice-differenced Fermat cone completion reaches beyond total exponent three halves](arithmetic/ABC_THREE_PRIME_FERMAT_NOISE.md) | proved | proved | For fixed exponent d and beta in [3/2,38/25), the specified three comparable power-sized prime factors give a weighted progression main term and signed error O(Q N^(-sigma+2 epsilon)), sigma=(3beta-4)/14. Two arithmetic differencing steps and the local four-shift estimate control the generic dual directions; exceptional directions are summed directly. |
| [False balanced radical incidences persist for three distinct primes beyond three halves](arithmetic/ABC_THREE_PRIME_FERMAT_NOISE.md) | proved | proved | For fixed d>=3 and total test exponent 3/2<=beta<38/25, for almost all ordered prime triples at the indicated scales there are at least a constant times N^(3-beta) distinct balanced pairwise coprime height-admissible dth-power radical triples with the same representatives at all primes and no integer equality. The radical budget is 3/d. |
| [Three or four homogeneous targets give uniform adaptive power-defect bounds](arithmetic/ABC_ADAPTIVE_HOMOGENEOUS_POWER_STARS.md) | proved | proved | For prescribed relative complete odds and fixed polynomial-height prime pool, a defect cap B for T1*T2/T3^2 at some q>=3 or T1*T2/(T3*T4) at some q>=2 gives O(B X^epsilon) witness tuples. A two-target fixed-q ratio has O(B X^(2/q+epsilon)) witnesses. A primitive height construction shows that three targets with weights 1,1,-2 cannot include q=2 in the subpower bound. |
| [Adaptive homogeneous stars count least target repair classes without affine conversion](arithmetic/ABC_ADAPTIVE_HOMOGENEOUS_POWER_STARS.md) | proved | proved | In the actual outside projection with a cheap target lock and small odds dictionaries, row-column separation modulo rth powers of the least target repairs gives normalized upper bounds max(c_V,c_U+c_V/2+2/(rL)) and max(c_V,c_U+2c_V/3+1/(rL)). This yields a strict saving at the symmetric minimum when liminf rL>18 and allows calibrated class dictionaries, without height restrictions on separating factors. |
| [A fixed letter gives half the smaller remaining radical cap](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL1. In primitive height shells with fixed complete T and bounded small-budget caps, the fixed-letter fibre exponent in base X^L is at most half the lesser free-letter outside radical cap after discounting any prescribed polynomial-height prime pools. At balanced caps the bound is 1/6 and complete dictionaries below 1/6 yield a strict saving, uniformly in valuation profiles. |
| [The fixed-letter exponent is strictly below both positive-scale masses](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL2. A positive limiting exponent d in a fixed-letter fibre is at most the smaller free-letter nonatomic mass and strictly below each free letter's mass at positive valuation scales, without any previous balance assumption. |
| [Each positive-scale mass exceeds one sixth close to minimum nonatomic mass](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL3. At balanced saturation and Gamma close to 1/2, each letter has mass above 1/6 by an absolute margin at a fixed positive cutoff. This is a fixed-fibre derivation of a consequence also available via the earlier individual atomic moment bound and tail control. |
| [A free letter's high-order escape or short height saves from the opposite nonatomic cap](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL4. A fixed-T exponent d satisfies d <= c_V(1-k e_U) for escaped numerical moment e_U of the other free letter, with a fixed positive k for bounded caps. If T and V are tall and U is short, replace e_U by 1-h_U. A cheap full divisor on U or a fixed real centre for V supplies the estimate. |
| [A balanced minimally repaired target radical has half-size exponent](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL5. For primitive radical balance band [a_-,a_+] and fixed least repair order M at height Y, multiplicity of a target radical R is at most R^(a_+/(2a_-)+arbitrarily small allowance). Thus the maximum is Y^((1/2+o(1))/M+epsilon) in balanced caps, and an exponent near 1/M requires target radicals with exponent at least (1/2-o(1))/M. |
| [Only the lower half of the normalized target multiplicity range can occur](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL8. With Z=Y^(1/M), the exact upper-tail formulation of the weighted target-support count need only be treated up to u=a_+/(2a_-)+arbitrarily small tolerance in the threshold m_Y(R)>=Z^u. A bound Z^(1-u-sigma+epsilon) on a sufficiently fine fixed mesh there is sufficient for a uniform saving, up to decreasing sigma. The weighted count bound conversely implies the tails. |
| [A fixed weighted least-repair class has an outside-radical fibre bound](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL6. In a primitive height shell with raw cap l_W L and prescribed class of the product of weighted least target repairs modulo Mth powers, b_W=min(l_W L,gcd(M,e_W)/M) is an outside exponent after deleting one reference support. The count exponent is at most min_T[b_T+min(b_U,b_V)/2]+eta L+epsilon. |
| [Joint valuation classes amplify effective orders through least common multiples](arithmetic/ABC_FIXED_LETTER_RADICAL_CAPS.md) | proved | proved | FL7. Classes of weighted original values or their least repairs induce exact valuation divisibility outside one reference support and above-tail coefficients. Independently cut off the least-repair constraints on each letter at B_W. If the retained effective orders have LCM at least K on all three letters, the joint count exponent is at most sum_W min(f_W,1/B_W)+3K^(-3/2)+epsilon, uniformly in list and weights. Complete-value classes have no tail cost. |
| [Near-quadratic additive graphs contain fixed binary shift allocations](arithmetic/ABC_ADDITIVE_TRANSLATION_CUBES.md) | proved | proved | TC1–TC2. For any fixed list of m choices of two out of three letters, a graph with E>=N^(2-eta) contains a translated additive base graph with part caps N and at least a constant times N^(2-4^m eta) edges, supporting all binary shift allocations among those pairs. Each output is an original edge and subset sums of shifts are distinct. |
| [Weighted least-repair classes on a translation cube have small fibres](arithmetic/ABC_ADDITIVE_TRANSLATION_CUBES.md) | proved | proved | TC3–TC4. Outside finitely many degenerate fibres, the distinct varying original values are nonproportional affine forms. A fixed weighted least-repair class modulo rth powers has O(X^(g/r+epsilon)) witnesses, with g the least gcd(r,e_j) among active forms. The choice of r and weights is unrestricted. |
| [A dense primitive arithmetic graph can forbid all three placements of one shift](arithmetic/ABC_ADDITIVE_TRANSLATION_CUBES.md) | proved | proved | A Behrend set of differences gives primitive additive graphs with part caps N and N^(2-o(1)) edges lacking even one simultaneous ternary placement of a nonzero shift. The examples impose primitivity and additivity and do not assert small radicals. |
| [Shifted original values keep their radicals outside prescribed pools](arithmetic/ABC_ADDITIVE_TRANSLATION_CUBES.md) | proved | proved | TC5. In balanced near-full cube fibres of part exponent 1/6, overlap of mass at least xi on any prescribed polynomial-height pool costs xi/2 in graph exponent. Pair determinants can be included in the pool, giving joint fresh radical exponent s/3-o(1) on s distinct varying forms. The balanced weighted repair class bound improves to g/(2r)+eta L+epsilon on a fixed fibre. |
| [Arithmetic derivatives impose a uniform lattice inequality on primitive families](arithmetic/ABC_ARITHMETIC_DERIVATIVE_FAMILY_LATTICES.md) | proved | proved | AD1. The primitive Wronskian gives a lower bound for each derivative outside the equal-logarithmic-derivative subspace. Eligible prime coordinate flags multiply this lower bound, then the resulting product is bounded by the Gram determinant divided by the full-rank minor gcd. Uniform in the number of rows. |
| [Valuation ranks at all depths divide arithmetic-derivative minors](arithmetic/ABC_ARITHMETIC_DERIVATIVE_FAMILY_LATTICES.md) | proved | proved | AD2. At each prime p and depth m form differences on the other two letters of basis rows having a p^m-divisible letter. The gcd of maximal minors has p-adic order at least the summed depthwise rank deficits, with one digit subtracted when p is a selected prime coordinate. The row-wise omitted color may vary. |
| [Common-modulus gains satisfy a projective capacity bound](arithmetic/ABC_ARITHMETIC_DERIVATIVE_FAMILY_LATTICES.md) | proved | proved | AD3–AD4. For three common moduli the numerator gain has exponent at most r-u_A, where the equal-logarithmic-derivative quotient uses the basis rows alone. This follows from the nonzero projective minor of any two distinct primitive rows and the two-color rank inequality. A separate two-row example makes the one-digit correction of AD2 sharp. |
| [Independent modular blocks test popular target radicals](arithmetic/ABC_MODULAR_TARGET_POPULARITY.md) | proved | proved | MP1. At polynomial height in N, T(H) <= E P_j(H) <= T(H/2)+N min(1,N^(2-beta+o(1))/H)^j, with beta the total prime exponent per block and independent blocks. For threshold N^u, any beta>2-u gives a power-small error after finitely many repetitions. Balanced least repair transfers with 2a_+/a_- in place of 2 before taking balance allowances. |
| [Bounded-height Fermat boxes give many popular false targets](arithmetic/ABC_MODULAR_TARGET_POPULARITY.md) | proved | proved | MP2–MP3. For the stated prime scales with 1<=beta<38/25, a proportion bounded below of tests has at least N^(min(1,3-3 beta/2))/log^2 N false target radicals of multiplicity at least cN^(2-beta). The fixed-target completion bound is O(N^2/Q+sqrt(Q) log^2 Q) from the smooth Fermat-curve sums. All representatives are fixed within each block. |
| [Several undersized modular popularity tests can share many false targets](arithmetic/ABC_MODULAR_TARGET_POPULARITY.md) | proved | proved | MP4. For j independent blocks of the stated Fermat types, the expected common false popular target count is at least N^(1-j(1-min(1,3-3 beta/2)))/log^(2j) N at threshold c N^(2-beta). This exceeds scale N^(beta-1) for beta<4(j+1)/(3j+2) in the indicated upper range, and for every fixed j when beta<=4/3. |
| [Pointwise prime-pool discounts permit every intermediate support multiplicity](arithmetic/ABC_TARGET_MULTIPLICITY_POINTWISE_OBSTRUCTION.md) | proved | proved | An abstract addition graph on finite-field evaluation labels has pair-unique edges, actual primitive balanced integer encodings, small radical and heights, and the fixed-label pointwise FL1 exponent for arbitrary prescribed polynomial-height pools. It has target exponent 1-u, multiplicity exponent u and total exponent one for any limiting u in [0,1/2]. Encodings can pass any fixed finite modulus while leaving at most one actual integer equality. |
| [Small affine minors for one complete letter force a global count saving](arithmetic/ABC_COMPLETE_LETTER_SMALL_FEATURES.md) | proved | proved | CF1. For any fixed feature rank bound R, at balanced individual radical caps and all sufficiently small budgets there is a uniform strict saving if one original letter is an exact affine function of integer features with all maximal affine minors at most X^theta_R. The proof treats both positive and zero nonatomic mass on the designated letter and does not require a supplied affordable record. |
| [Bounded-rank progressions and short approximate carriers give global savings](arithmetic/ABC_COMPLETE_LETTER_SMALL_FEATURES.md) | proved | proved | Small-minor complete-letter counting extends to fixed-rank progression boxes of small numerical volume, polynomial features of fixed degree and dimension, and affine approximations with error X^theta for sufficiently small fixed theta. Every balanced saturated endpoint requires a positive normalized exponent in rank-one interval bins and in each bounded-rank cover by admissible carriers. |
| [Bounded additive doubling is excluded on a complete letter at all balanced profiles](arithmetic/ABC_COMPLETE_LETTER_SMALL_FEATURES.md) | proved | proved | For any fixed K, a complete-letter dictionary with doubling at most K yields a uniform power saving in balanced caps. On a saturated subfamily with comparable complete-value fibre sizes, its additive energy is o(\|S\|^3). The latter is qualitative and allows growing doubling with zero normalized exponent. |
| [Valuation projections count low-rank rational cosets with a radical cap](arithmetic/ABC_VALUATION_SPAN_COSETS.md) | proved | proved | VS1. At polynomial height, the number of rational tuples in a coset of multiplicative rank at most (log X)^kappa and joint radical at most X^rho is at most X^((1-1/kappa)_+ rho+epsilon), with no bound on the coset representative or generators. The exponent is sharp for general integer dictionaries. |
| [Separating prime pools give global savings for original letters and primitive ratios](arithmetic/ABC_VALUATION_SPAN_COSETS.md) | proved | proved | VS2–VS3. A prescribed prime pool separating one complete letter or pair ratio, with sublogarithmic sum of p^(-a) at fixed a<1, gives deficits (1-a)/(6(2+a)) and (1-a)/(3(1+2a)) from the coefficient 1/3, respectively, up to fixed allowances. In particular each fixed polylogarithmic rank gives a uniform saving on a prescribed multiplicative coset. |
| [Separating prime sets have limited fractional packing at balanced saturation](arithmetic/ABC_VALUATION_SPAN_COSETS.md) | proved | proved | VS4–VS7. A separating prime set contributes expected log radical at least the marginal entropy up to height subpower errors. Fractional coordinate-basis packing on any one complete letter or pair ratio has weight at most 2+o(1) at balanced saturation. Edmonds–Fulkerson implies a rank-deficient A with \|E\A\| <= (2+o(1))(r(E)-r(A)). |
| [Three disjoint separating prime sets give coefficient two sevenths](arithmetic/ABC_VALUATION_SPAN_COSETS.md) | proved | proved | VS8. For arbitrary small-budget profiles, a fractional packing of weight P>=2 gives coefficient max(1/4,2/(P+4)) for a single complete letter and min(1/P,2/(P+4)) for a pair ratio. Packings of weight at least P on all three letters or all three pair ratios give coefficient at most 2/(3P). No bound on valuation rank is required. |
| [Fixed-fold rational products at polynomial height already have maximal exponent](arithmetic/ABC_VALUATION_SPAN_COSETS.md) | proved | proved | Prime sign coloring and fixed-fold divisor bounds give \|A^(m)\| >= \|A\|^m X^(-o(1)) for any positive rational dictionary of polynomial height and fixed m. Thus the large-product alternative in the few-prime sum-product results of Agrawal, Bloom and Petridis does not by itself constrain the sparse primitive arithmetic graph. |
| [One crossing prime gives a relative-interval radical count](arithmetic/ABC_SHORT_INTERVAL_RADICAL_FILTER.md) | proved | proved | SI1. At fixed small budget L and cap X^(L ell), any relative window of size X^(-tau) contains at most X^((1-tau/2+eta)L ell+epsilon) positive integers up to X. Recover the smaller charged side of one prime and the remaining cofactor after the greedy prefix. |
| [A sufficiently short power interval contains very few small-radical integers](arithmetic/ABC_SHORT_INTERVAL_RADICAL_FILTER.md) | proved | proved | SI2. For every A,eta>0 there is a fixed positive theta giving count X^(eta L+epsilon) in any relative interval of width X^(-1+theta) under radical cap X^(AL), for all sufficiently small fixed L. On a numerical shell of positive height, this applies to sufficiently short absolute power intervals and gives X^(eta/k+epsilon) for fixed sufficiently large k-fullness. |
| [A short real filter lowers the sufficient prime-block exponent to one minus multiplicity exponent](arithmetic/ABC_SHORT_INTERVAL_RADICAL_FILTER.md) | proved | proved | SI3. With free radical caps N^a and fixed target height shell, the short numerical near-equality filter leaves at most N^(a+eta+o(1)) free support pairs per target radical. At threshold N^u and block exponent beta the false popular target error is N min(1,N^(a+eta-beta-u+o(1)))^j. Balanced a near one permits beta>1-u with fixed margins. |
| [Fractional prime projections pay their average conditional entropy loss](arithmetic/ABC_APPROXIMATE_VALUATION_SEPARATORS.md) | proved | proved | AV1–AV2. A packing of prime loads at most one and total weight P bounds the entropy of a complete letter or primitive ratio by its expected radical cost divided by P plus the average conditional entropy of the projections. The fixed-letter and two-letter estimates yield the stated arbitrary-profile exponents with the additive loss confined to the entropy branch. |
| [A logarithmic missing valuation rank is free at exponent scale](arithmetic/ABC_APPROXIMATE_VALUATION_SEPARATORS.md) | proved | proved | AV3. A selector whose valuation kernel has rank O((log X)^kappa) costs at most beta_kappa times the expected outside radical logarithm in conditional entropy, up to allowances. Consequently packing weight P acts as P/(1+(P-1) beta_kappa). In particular three disjoint selectors missing O(log X) dimensions still give 2/7. |
| [Near-natural prime frequencies alone do not extract cheap valuation projections](arithmetic/ABC_APPROXIMATE_VALUATION_SEPARATORS.md) | proved | proved | The evaluation-code model obeys the fixed-target and ordinary prime frequency constraints. Any cheap-prime separating pool only captures a power-smaller family, while two complementary exact separators exist for each pair ratio and the coordinate rank remains large. Logarithmic-rank-deficiency selectors have near-one packing in this model. Actual integer equality is not asserted. |

## Formal verification

Formal developments and characteristic-zero Hopf/Image classifications: complete even-start purity via marked Davenport-Zannier pairs, Fuss-Catalan geometric counts and exact field descent; all-height safety and sharp degree/prime thresholds.

**Authored assessment:** Formal scope varies by project. GMC2 is conditional on two named axiom interfaces; binary GVC and full generic discriminant geometry remain partial.

[Topic guide](foundations/README.md)

**Computed obligations:** 17 unresolved; 4 resolved within their exact scope.

| Principal result | Authored state | Graph status | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| [GVC counterexamples and binary supporting algebra](foundations/formal/gvc/README.md) | partial | proved | The ternary counterexample and profile family have Lean proofs. Binary GVC has supporting formal algebra but is not an end-to-end Lean theorem. |
| [Binary Gaussian moments in Lean](foundations/formal/gmc2/README.md) | proved | conditional | The complete bivariate theorem is formalized conditional on the explicit Duistermaat–van der Kallen and finite-type specialization axiom interfaces. |
| [Characteristic-zero finite etale Keller construction](foundations/formal/finite-etale-keller/README.md) | proved | proved | The focused paper certificate proves the construction, Jacobian normalization, full fibre and naturality; the supplied-presentation extension and analytic counting remain outside this certificate. |
| [Tangent-pencil algebra in Lean](foundations/formal/discriminant-pencils/README.md) | partial | proved | Axiom-free modules verify the stated tangent, contact and collision algebra. The full generic geometric manuscript theorem remains a written argument. |
| [Primitive quadratic norms and binary correlations in Lean](foundations/formal/quadratic-norms/README.md) | partial | proved | Lean proves the four primitive-value criteria, local exclusions, split-prime descent, and all four primitive sumset classifications through their published finite scan cutoffs. It proves the −8 dyadic and selected-shell decompositions, the inert target-prime count, signed lattice and representation bounds, large-prime bad-count estimates, and the progression and Euler bounds for the selected-shell sieve. It verifies all 107 −8 interval margins, including the searched divisor envelopes and recomputed prime bounds, and combines these with the uniform onsets, finite scan, and descent. It proves the surviving-coordinate counting bound and the weighted norm estimate for the nonnegative dyadic kernel. It checks the −8 coefficient lists through the Sturm cutoffs and derives the three unrestricted −8 sumsets and the ordered-pair lower bound from the theta identities, unramified coefficient data, and finite Hecke orbit hypotheses. It checks the −11 rational interval margins and proves the inert-prime and Euler bounds, the odd-shell identities, and the arithmetic sieve inequality above the −11 cutoff. It proves the lattice, representation, and large inert-prime shell counts. It derives the filtered cusp error from Hecke coefficient data, proves the small-prime bound at inert primes dividing the target, and verifies the numerical spectral deductions at auxiliary unit levels. | [Exact weighted volume test at nonzero angular roots](foundations/extended-geometry/SPHERICAL_WEIGHTED_PUISEUX_VOLUME.md) | proved | proved | At a finite nonzero angular root, the squared bounded-phase volume is finite exactly when the sum of Puiseux branch contacts truncated at the differential pole threshold D is strictly below Dn at each branch. | [Exact interval moments of bilateral automorphic sphere phases](foundations/extended-geometry/SPHERICAL_BILATERAL_AUTOMORPHIC_MOMENTS.md) | proved | proved | The stated polynomial sphere automorphism preserves the moment functional, giving exact univariate moments, divergent bounded-phase volume, and an absolute nonpower family of least sphere degree 18h with explicit prime-power poles. |
